nodes.label: Link Publico do Diretor - Checkpoint Semanal
nodes.rationale: Hoje so existe link publico por equipe (/daily/:slug). O plano adiciona um link publico por diretor exibindo o card Checkpoint Semanal com todos os gerentes daquele diretor, reusando exatamente a UI de /checkpoint.
nodes.norm_label: link publico do diretor - checkpoint semanal

nodes.label: Edge Function director-weekly
nodes.rationale: Funcao publica com service role em supabase/functions/director-weekly/index.ts, registrada em supabase/config.toml com verify_jwt = false porque a pagina publica nao autentica. Recebe { slug, week_start? }, resolve o diretor em brokers (role=director, active), agrega daily_team_reports + daily_broker_entries da semana seg-dom e le checkpoint_targets. Isolamento deliberado: nao expoe dados de outros diretores.

nodes.label: Pagina publica PublicDirectorCheckpoint
nodes.rationale: Rota /diretor/:slug registrada em src/App.tsx antes do RequireAuth, portanto fora da autenticacao. Nao exige PIN porque sao dados agregados de leitura apenas. Header identico ao /checkpoint (navegacao de semana + Hoje) para consistencia visual.

nodes.label: DirectorFunnelCard (componente extraido)
nodes.rationale: Extraido de src/pages/Checkpoint.tsx para src/components/checkpoint/DirectorFunnelCard.tsx com o objetivo unico de reuso na pagina publica, explicitamente sem mudanca visual.

nodes.label: TeamCheckpointCard (componente extraido)
nodes.rationale: Extraido de Checkpoint.tsx para src/components/checkpoint/TeamCheckpointCard.tsx; renderizado no modal aberto pelo botao Ver gerentes, mantendo a mesma UI ja existente.

nodes.label: Pagina Checkpoint (src/pages/Checkpoint.tsx)
nodes.rationale: Fonte original dos cards de checkpoint; sofre refatoracao pequena para consumir os componentes extraidos em vez de definilos inline.

nodes.label: AdminDailyTeams - secao Diretores
nodes.rationale: Nova secao lista cada diretor com URL https://crm-faceimob.com.br/diretor/<slug> e botao copiar, seguindo o mesmo padrao ja usado nos links de equipe para nao introduzir uma segunda convencao de UI.

nodes.label: Convencao de slug (slugify sobre broker.name)
nodes.rationale: Reusa a mesma funcao slugify de AdminDailyTeams.tsx aplicada em broker.name, garantindo que o slug gerado no admin e o slug resolvido na edge function coincidam.

nodes.label: Acesso publico sem autenticacao nem PIN
nodes.rationale: Trade-off aceito: rota fora do RequireAuth e verify_jwt = false, sem PIN, porque o payload e agregado e somente leitura; o isolamento de dados e garantido no servidor filtrando por director_id.
nodes.norm_label: acesso publico sem autenticacao nem pin

nodes.label: Agregacao semanal seg-dom de relatorios diarios
nodes.rationale: Combina daily_team_reports e daily_broker_entries na janela semanal segunda a domingo e compara com checkpoint_targets (global ou por team) para produzir os numeros do funil.
nodes.norm_label: agregacao semanal seg-dom de relatorios diarios

nodes.label: Politica de crawlers (robots.txt)
nodes.rationale: Allow: / para todos os agentes, com entradas explicitas para Googlebot, Bingbot, Twitterbot e facebookexternalhit; os dois ultimos existem para permitir que os unfurlers busquem as meta tags OG - nenhum caminho e bloqueado, inclusive as rotas publicas /daily e /diretor.

nodes.label: Lovable Project Platform
nodes.rationale: Project is hosted/edited through Lovable; edits in Lovable auto-commit to the repo and pushed local changes reflect back, so the repo and the Lovable workspace are two views of the same source. Deploy is Share -> Publish, custom domain via Project > Settings > Domains.

nodes.norm_label: frontend tech stack (vite, typescript, react, shadcn-ui, tailwind css)

nodes.label: Four-Phase Seed Against the New Schema
nodes.rationale: Loads catalogo, fictional login-blocked people, teams, leads, deals, CCA, SDR, daily, gamification, marketing and workspace. Records are idempotent so the command can be re-run safely.
nodes.norm_label: four-phase seed against the new schema

nodes.label: npm run db:seed:remote
nodes.rationale: Runs psql inside Docker specifically so the password is never placed in the connection URI nor in terminal history; the password is prompted without being echoed.

nodes.label: npm run user:create (first real user bootstrap)
nodes.rationale: Reads VITE_SUPABASE_URL from .env and prompts (without echo) for the initial password and the service_role key, so the privileged key is used once at bootstrap and never persisted.
nodes.norm_label: npm run user:create (first real user bootstrap)

nodes.label: service_role Key Must Never Reach the Vite .env or the Browser
nodes.rationale: The key is copied from Supabase -> Project Settings -> API Keys at use time. Anything in a Vite .env is bundled into client code, so storing it there, committing it, or exposing it in the browser would hand full-privilege database access to any visitor.
nodes.norm_label: service_role key must never reach the vite .env or the browser

nodes.label: Schema Novo (greenfield FACEIMOB backend)
nodes.rationale: Modeled from zero out of the 14/07 and 23/07 meeting notes plus what the current frontend requires; nothing was imported from the previous database. Migrations are creation-only (no DROP) because the target is a brand-new empty project. 58 tables, 123 policies, 70 functions, 69 test asserts.

nodes.label: scripts/validate-schema.sh --all (disposable Postgres harness)
nodes.rationale: Validates without deploying anything: applies every migration to a throwaway Postgres and runs the behavior asserts. Requires only Docker and deliberately avoids the Supabase CLI. Fails if a migration does not apply, if any table in public lacks RLS, or if any behavior assert breaks.

nodes.label: supabase/seed.sql (mandatory catalog seed)
nodes.rationale: Loads the catalog the product cannot run without: pipeline stages, document types, shifts, general queue, scoring rules and permissions.

nodes.label: Stale project_id in supabase/config.toml
nodes.rationale: config.toml still points at wkgvqzcqtgyugzykxunj, the old project. The project_id must be swapped for the new project ref before running db push, otherwise the push targets the legacy database.

nodes.label: CRUD Audit (six findings)
nodes.rationale: Run after the schema was finished, confronting the real policy matrix against what each screen needs. All six findings were reproduced in a failing test before being fixed, with regressions kept in tests/03_crud_audit.sql. Findings: broker could change own bypass_ip_check and own status; broker could not check out of own shift; manually created deal was born without a participant (invisible and uneditable, and the INSERT failed outright with supabase-js .select()); broker could inject a comment into another team's lead by passing the UUID; deal_clients DELETE was governed by the read rule and was more permissive than INSERT/UPDATE.

nodes.label: RLS Filters Rows, Not Columns
nodes.rationale: Root cause shared by audit findings 1 and 2. The profiles_update_self policy releases the whole row, so a row-level policy can never protect an individual administrative column; guarding a field requires a trigger instead.

nodes.label: profiles_guard_admin_columns()
nodes.rationale: Trigger that blocks a broker from self-editing administrative columns (bypass_ip_check, status) which row-level RLS cannot protect.

nodes.label: INSERT ... RETURNING Evaluates the SELECT Policy Before AFTER Triggers Fire
nodes.rationale: An AFTER INSERT trigger cannot fix visibility of a freshly inserted deal: Postgres evaluates the SELECT policy against the new row before AFTER triggers run, so deal_participants is still empty at that instant. Visibility had to be changed to read created_by off the row itself.
nodes.norm_label: insert ... returning evaluates the select policy before after triggers fire

nodes.label: Deliberately Write-Free Immutable Log Tables
nodes.rationale: Verified end state: no table has DELETE more permissive than INSERT/UPDATE, and five tables have no write policy at all because they are immutable logs - lead_events, lead_assignments, deal_history, cca_case_events, sdr_messages - all written exclusively by SECURITY DEFINER functions.

nodes.label: Roles Are N:N (user_roles)
nodes.rationale: Explicit requirement: a director may also act as manager and broker. The old schema duplicated the role in two places, which is what caused Rafael to receive a CCA notification without holding the role.

nodes.label: auth_visible_profiles()
nodes.rationale: Single source of truth for visibility: broker sees only himself, manager sees the team, director sees the teams he directs, admin/socio see everyone. Leads, deals, metrics and targets all filter through it, so changing the hierarchy rule means editing one place.

nodes.label: deal_participants (replaces broker1/2/3 and manager1/2/3)
nodes.rationale: The hard limit of 3 was arbitrary and made any per-broker aggregation impossible, so the fixed columns became rows.

nodes.label: VGV Split Computed in the Database, Always Closing at 100%
nodes.rationale: The rateio is calculated in the database rather than the client so it always sums to 100%, including the three-broker case (33.334/33.333/33.333) where naive rounding would lose a thousandth.
nodes.norm_label: vgv split computed in the database, always closing at 100%

nodes.label: deal_clients (ordinal 1 or 2)
nodes.rationale: The 12 duplicated second-buyer fields became rows distinguished by ordinal, removing the parallel column set.

nodes.label: deal_documents (typed and versioned)
nodes.rationale: Replaces the single attachment field. Re-sending a document does not erase the previous one: it is marked as superseded and carries a version, which is the change history the CCA team asked for.

nodes.label: No Password or Token in the Public Schema
nodes.rationale: Authentication is 100% Supabase Auth. Secrets live outside anything PostgREST can reach, so a policy mistake cannot leak credentials.
nodes.norm_label: no password or token in the public schema

nodes.label: private.integration_credentials
nodes.rationale: API tokens live in a schema PostgREST does not expose; the admin writes them via RPC and never receives the value back, so the token is write-only from the application's perspective.

nodes.label: Public Link PIN Stored as bcrypt Hash
nodes.rationale: The PIN protecting public daily links is never stored in clear text, so leaking the row does not grant access to the link.
nodes.norm_label: public link pin stored as bcrypt hash

nodes.label: Anonymous Surface Is Exactly Three Functions
nodes.rationale: No table is readable by anon; the entire unauthenticated attack surface is three RPCs, which bounds what a leaked anon key can do.
nodes.norm_label: anonymous surface is exactly three functions

nodes.label: closed_months (closed month locks editing)
nodes.rationale: Prevents a past report from changing retroactively - the direct answer to the complaint about discrepancies in the annual numbers.

nodes.label: cca_stages (configurable CCA stages)
nodes.rationale: Created because the frontend already used it and it did not exist; deliberately follows the same pattern as pipeline_stages.

nodes.label: Lead Roleta with 5-Minute Attendance Lock
nodes.rationale: A lead assigned by the roulette is locked to the broker for 5 minutes; the lock only fires if expired leads are actively released, so the mechanism depends on a scheduled sweep.

nodes.label: release_expired_leads()
nodes.rationale: Must run roughly every 30 seconds (pg_cron or Vercel Cron). Without the cron the 5-minute attendance lock never releases, so the roulette silently stops recycling leads. Still pending.

nodes.label: perform_checkin(ip)
nodes.rationale: Receives the caller IP so the allowed-IP lock is enforced server-side rather than trusted from the client.

nodes.rationale: Marked as replaceable by the public RPCs instead of being rewritten.
